play_name: Leave room to see if effort comes back
behavioral_target: Carrying all the effort of reaching out, planning, and giving in a close relationship.
trigger: You want connection. You notice you are the one who texts, plans, and gives most of the time.
old_play: You reach out first, make the plans, and give more, so the connection keeps going from your side.
function_of_old_play: Doing the effort keeps you two connected right now instead of letting things go quiet.
new_play: Notice when you are always the one giving effort. Sometimes hold back and leave room. Match your giving to what comes back, and see if they reach out or give too.
what_to_expect: It may feel uncomfortable to hold back. You might see they step up, or you might see they don't. Either way you learn something real.
why_supports_task: Intentional Investment means both people choose to invest. Leaving room lets you see if the effort goes both ways before you give more.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Always texting first; always making the plans; always giving more than you receive.
context_limitations: Reaching out and giving are good. This is about balance, not going cold or keeping score. You still get to be warm when it is mutual.
review_reason: Reciprocity function is partly inferred; meaning depends on the balance of effort over time.

behavioral_target: Carrying all the relational work — starting things and fixing every problem — in an established relationship.
trigger: Something needs to start or a problem needs solving. You notice you are always the one who does it.
old_play: You initiate and you fix everything yourself, so things keep running.
function_of_old_play: Doing it all keeps the relationship going and stops problems from just sitting there.
new_play: When something needs starting or fixing, pause before you jump in. Name it out loud and leave room for the other person to help.
what_to_expect: Problems may sit longer. The other person may not step in. You may feel the pull to just handle it yourself.
why_supports_task: Integration means building a shared life where the load is carried together. Pausing lets you see if the work can be shared, or stays only on you.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Always being the one to initiate; always being the one to fix everything.
context_limitations: Starting things and helping are good. Some things really do need you. This is about balance, not about doing nothing.
review_reason: Function partly inferred; meaning depends on the balance of who carries the work.

play_name: Say it once instead of storing it up
behavioral_target: Silently tracking what feels unfair instead of naming it.
trigger: Something feels unfair or one-sided. Instead of saying it, you add it to a running list in your head.
old_play: You keep score of what they have done and what you have done.
function_of_old_play: Keeping score keeps a record of what feels unfair so it is not forgotten.
new_play: When something feels unfair, name that one thing out loud soon after. Ask for what you need instead of storing it.
what_to_expect: Speaking up feels risky. They may not respond the way you hope. But the unfair thing gets a chance to be worked on.
why_supports_task: Integration means working through problems as a team. Naming one thing at a time lets it be solved instead of piling up into resentment.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Keeping score of wrongs and what feels unfair.
context_limitations: Noticing unfairness is okay. This is about voicing it early, not swallowing it or listing it all at once.
review_reason: Single-behavior Play; function inferred from the Resentment context of the cluster.
